title: Tughlaq

vibeProfile.oneLine: A visionary medieval sultan's descent into tyranny, in a landmark Indian play.

summary: Tughlaq is Girish Karnad's acclaimed play, originally in Kannada, about the fourteenth-century Delhi sultan Muhammad bin Tughlaq, a brilliant, idealistic and ultimately tyrannical ruler whose visionary schemes collapse into chaos and bloodshed. Widely read as an allegory of the disillusionment of post-independence India, it is a masterful historical drama about idealism turning to cruelty. One of the landmark plays of modern Indian theatre, it established Karnad as a major dramatist.
whyReadIt: Karnad's masterful play on a brilliant, doomed medieval sultan, and an allegory of post-independence disillusion.

funFacts.text: The play is often read as an allegory for the disillusionment of India in the years after independence.
